Rust is the game that makes you want to take an angle grinder to your fingertips.
First, seconds after spawning on the beach, you’re chased by naked players shouting slurs. Second, only about 5% of the player base seems to speak English. The other 95% speak what sounds like a mix of Chinese and Russian, often very loudly.
Do not buy this game if you want to preserve your sanity. While playing, I missed some major world news. I only just found out that the Queen had died and that a pandemic called COVID-19 had occurred. I’m sure Vladimir Putin had a key role in developing this game to mentally disturb Russian players even more than they already are.
And don’t get me started on China. Its population seems unmatched. I’ve never seen anything like it: you can join a server with three players, type one word in Chinese, and an entire colony will arrive promptly.
This game has also introduced me to same-sex marriage; I’ve seen several examples during my time playing this mentally challenging and physically demanding game.
I’ve gone through 16 mice, 9 keyboards, and around 23 monitors for the reasons stated above.
Save yourself, and do not buy this game.

The game itself isn't bad, in fact it's actually quite fun, but it's hard to recommend because the community is easily the most toxic I've ever experienced. The building mechanics are interesting, and even normal competition between players and groups can be pretty fun too. If you can find a couple friends to play with it might be worth it, if not, probably just play something else with a community that's less hostile. Kill or be killed is fine enough, and I could accept people killing you for resources, but the lengths many players go to inflict suffering on others, with no personal benefit makes me think the game is mostly a haven for sadists and psychopaths.

Fun game, but unfortunately the developer focus is on adding pay to win features rather than fix the horrible issues with cheating. It is borderline unplayable with the amount of users on every server which have more information than you, the ability to fly up walls, and shoot you with inhuman skills from the other side of the map. Instead of making any sort of acknowledgement, each month adds more pay to win features to the game and no improvements to the useless anti cheat.

In it's current state the game is certainly a lot of fun and with the frequent updates the developer has shown they are working on creating a better experience.

Quick Takes
- Performance could be better. There are many settings but the optimization just isn't there yet.
- Killing other people and hearing their screams is satisfying.
- Building is a ton of fun!
- Gathering/Salvaging never truly stops however for me it is relaxing.
- Animals are glitchy as hell near rocks, changes in elevation, building, etc and it doesn't appear they will be fixed anytime soon.
- Playing with friends is optimal but solo play is possible.
- No character customization. Whatever you start as you are stuck with forever. On every server. Until they hopefully change it..
- Crafting system is good but not great. More variety would be welcome.
- Crafting skins can be expensive
This game is a lot of fun to build a base and the way the wipes are set up it prevents MEGA bases.

Before the recoil update Rust was actually a fun, competetive game. The game took skill to master recoil, gamesense, basebuilding etc. Even tho Rust always had their problems/bugs and game changing updates like the (compound bow bp) it has been a great experience and a great game, but currently my well known Rust has changed...The changing recoil made the game (non competetive) and more (casual) which many gamers sees as a good and positive thing, but I bought Rust bc it was described as a hardcore survival game, not the one winning a fight by luck/no skill and bloom which the current update (recoil update) gave us. The recoil is easier and can be mastered 100x faster than before and new players can outskill old veterans by just playing a couple of weeks learning the recoil. Of course gamesense matters aswell but Rust have been especially known for its hard recoil. Maybe the update gave new players a chance winning fights but the time (old players) spent on the game does not matter anymore. What about my 2000 hours learning the ak-spray. Gone for nothing? Atleast give the community no bloom and keep the game competetive with easier recoil like now. Btw Im traumatized by animal attacks!

LATEST UPDATE TO RUST

Why are you hitting that rock? To survive? To make something you need in the world?… no… to get XP.
Why are you killing that animal? To eat? To prolong your meagre existence?… no… to make a flashing star pop up and a bong noise happen
How did you learn to make that item? By finding another in the world? By discovering an object that youve risked your precious life to go and find? By exploring and interacting? Trading even? Practicing something related?…. no, I hit a rock repeatedly… oh, and I dropped an axe ages ago. (?)
Do I care if I die?… No, it was worth it for the xp.
Don't buy this game, it will take up 1000s of hours each month once you really start playing...

Blueprint system was amazing with the fragments was way better back in 2015, even XP wasn't that bad.

Recoil from the AK I wish was the same in the old experimental, but now it's "learnable" which I guess is better than having that awful recoil comp.

All in all, I guess it's a good game and I do recommend those who haven't to try it, it is just a shame you won't be able to play it back when Gazza was in charge and Rust was at it's best (imo).
But the current system with workbenches and scrap is alright currently.

The game has in my opinion one of the steepest learning curves of any game. But, if you're willing to invest the time into understanding the game and how it works it can be one of the most enjoyable experiences gaming has to offer. The game's main core mechanics that i recommend any new player to focus on learning would be the recoil of guns, how the monuments and the scrap system works, and figuring out what loot is more valuable than others. The game has lots of things that make it unique, from a proximity push to talk, to special servers dedicated specifically to pvp, role play, and more. There's also tons of events that you can attempt to take down such as the attack helicopter, the bradley tank in launch site, oil rigs, underwater labs and underground train systems, and even random air drops that can contain valuable loot. overall id give this game a 8.5/10, its one of the best games to get into especially if you have friends that are all looking to do something new, or just need to take a break from your standard game

Rust is a pretty good game tbh. I've tried several survival games and found that Rust is the most enjoyable one for me. The building system is vast, there are a few bugs but it's understanable considering it's still in alpha. Recently a car spawn command has been added for admins, you can spawn a car and drive it around, it's great fun tbh. Also I like the idea that you can be attacked by helicopters, but with admin perms you can just fly up to it and shoot that thing down xD. I like how this game is constantly being improved, you can now sit on chairs and increase your comfort level. I continue to have so much fun on this, I've built all sorts of buildings from a prison to a base on an iceburg.
I definitely recommend this game if you love building random shit, pvping or just exploring. You can explore all sorts from, caves, to power plants.
